with_model_gateway.description:
Search the books you may read now (needs read; agents also need activate for instruction passages).
        Results carry citation handles for open_citation. Optional filters narrow the evidence before ranking:
        `book` (slugs), `path` (prefix, e.g. "data/"), `origin` (kstd origins: human, assisted, model, tool, unknown),
        `acceptance` (how the book's current version was accepted: curator_passkey, operator_cli, consumer_attested, policy,
        none; notes are not filtered), `current_only` (kstd validity includes now), `context` ({platform, version}, e.g. {"platform": "vcenter",
        "version": "7.0.3"}: a file whose kstd applies_to the context contradicts is left out; `item.scope` says
        unbounded, match or needs_context). `max_chars` (80-4800) makes each text a snippet around the
        match with `truncated`; open_citation gives the full passage. Use it in agent loops. `_meta`
        "kutuphane/retrieval" says which model stages ran (embedding, translation, rerank: ok, failed, skipped).
with_model_gateway.name: search_library

with_model_gateway.description:
Open a citation handle: the exact passage of that version, if you may read it now (needs read on the
        book; agents also need activate for an instruction passage). A note reference (book@nt_…) gives the note,
        with `current` in the optional context (repo, branch, path, commit, platform, version).
with_model_gateway.name: open_citation

with_model_gateway.description:
Answer from the library with [n] citations, or status not_in_library (needs read on the books it
            uses). The optional filters are those of search_library. With `background: true` it returns {job_id,
            status: queued} at once: poll job_status, then job_result. An `idempotency_key` (8-128 characters) makes
            a retried submission return the same job. `retrieval` says which model stages of the search ran
            (embedding, translation, rerank: ok, failed, skipped).
with_model_gateway.name: ask_library

with_model_gateway.description: Show your stored answer and its evidence again (needs read on its books now; no model call).
with_model_gateway.name: reopen_answer

with_model_gateway.description: Read a text document of a specific version (needs read on the book; agent instructions need activate).
with_model_gateway.name: read_document

with_model_gateway.description:
The books and journals you may read now (needs read; a book you may not read is not named): kind (book
        or journal), the current content_id and profile_id, and its publication (acceptance: kind, by, at,
        legacy; the channel ingest or import; for a package the issuer key and the sequence).
with_model_gateway.name: list_books

with_model_gateway.description:
The files of a book's current version, a page at a time (needs read on the book): path, digest, size,
        passage count and the kstd item (license, ai_use, personal_data, origin, validity, applies_to). Pass
        `next_cursor` as `cursor` for the next page; read_document reads a text file.
with_model_gateway.name: list_files

with_model_gateway.description:
The state of your background ask_library job (no grant; your own jobs only): queued, running,
            succeeded, failed or cancelled.
with_model_gateway.name: job_status

with_model_gateway.description: The answer of your succeeded job, as reopen_answer shows it (needs read on its books now).
with_model_gateway.name: job_result

with_model_gateway.description:
Cancel your background job (no grant; your own jobs only): a queued job stops at once; a running one
            before its model call or its result.
with_model_gateway.name: job_cancel

with_model_gateway.description:
Write a note into a journal (needs propose). kind: finding, decision_proposal, dead_end, convention,
        lesson, test_result. citations: passage handles or code citations repo@commit:path:start-end[#symbol].
        links: [{type, ref}] (derived_from, supersedes, same_as, contradicts, about, fixed_by, violates,
        decided_by) to older notes (book@nt_…) or passages. decision (decision_proposal only): {options: the 2..20
        options offered, in order; choice: the one chosen}. The note starts pending; only a curator approves it.
        The same bytes again are the same note (recurrence + 1). Give an idempotency_key to retry safely.
        applies_to: the platforms and the version range (e.g. ">=7,<8") the note holds for; a reader gives its
        platform and version in the query context.
with_model_gateway.name: propose_note

with_model_gateway.description:
Link a note (src, book@nt_…; needs propose on its book) to a note or passage (dst; needs read):
        same_as (same book), contradicts, about, fixed_by, violates, decided_by. The same link again is kept once.
with_model_gateway.name: link_notes

with_model_gateway.description:
Check code citations (`repo@commit:path:start-end[#symbol]`) of a journal's repositories against `at`
        (a branch name or a full commit id): verified, stale (with moved_to), missing, or unverifiable with a
        reason. No code text is returned. Needs read on the book.
with_model_gateway.name: verify_citations

with_model_gateway.description:
List agent notes in the journals you may read (needs read on each journal): fast SQL filters, no model
        call. `sets`: current (approved, in your context), open (pending, not accepted), history. Context: repo,
        branch, path (or `paths`: up to 20, each item names the paths it matches), commit, platform and version
        (a note with `applies_to` needs them, as files do). `refs` (up to 50 note
        references): only these notes, each with `standing` and `standing_seq`. Use `since` with the last watermark to
        get changes and `left` tombstones; `cursor` for the next page. `min_passed` (0..100): only notes with at least
        that many `passed` outcomes; `exclude_failed`: no note whose latest outcome is failed or reverted.
with_model_gateway.name: query_notes

with_model_gateway.description:
The notes linked to a note reference or a passage handle (depth 1 or 2), only those you may read (needs
        read on their journals) and that are in `sets` in your context (repo, branch, path, commit, platform,
        version).
with_model_gateway.name: neighbours

with_model_gateway.description:
Record how an item worked in a task (needs propose and read on its book). ref: a note (book@nt_…) or a
        passage handle; both name one exact version. task_ref: your task or run id. result: passed, failed,
        reverted or reopened. Outcomes are counts on the item; they never change its Standing. A retry with the
        same idempotency_key returns the first receipt.
with_model_gateway.name: record_outcome

with_model_gateway.description:
Ask the person to confirm whose words a note holds (D70 R3; needs read on the note's book). Only the
        person can confirm, in curator web with a passkey; this tool never confirms. Returns {ref, origin,
        confirmation: {state: open, confirmed, expired or none, url?, expires_at?, claim?, entered_by?,
        confirmed_by?}}. Show the url to the person.
with_model_gateway.name: confirm_origin

with_model_gateway.description:
Submit a signed Kütüphane package (base64 of the tar that `kutuphane export` writes; needs propose on the
        book that its manifest names). The same checks as `kutuphane receive` run: a trusted, unrevoked key, the
        signature, every digest, a newer sequence. Nothing is published: a person approves it with
        `kutuphane approve-import`. Returns the import status: received, findings, approved or refused.
with_model_gateway.name: submit_package

with_model_gateway.description:
The status of a package that you submitted (no grant; your own submissions only): received, findings (a person reads them before approval),
        approved (published) or refused (with the reasons).
with_model_gateway.name: package_status
